vehicles.headline: Lower purchase price; published three-across test in related Exceed trim.
vehicles.summary: The original ZM LS is a petrol alternative to the PHEV. BabyDrive fitted three forward-facing restraints in an Exceed; confirm them in the LS. Row three has no top tethers. No home charger is needed.

range.basis: Electric range does not apply to this petrol configuration.

battery.basis: No traction battery; conventional petrol drivetrain.

depletedConsumption.basis: Charge-depleted PHEV consumption does not apply.

vehicles.batteryWarranty: No high-voltage traction battery. Standard 12-V battery terms differ from the vehicle warranty.

consumption.basis: Manufacturer combined ADR 81/02 claim for LS FWD seven-seat; not the ES five-seat 7.5 figure. Local family use can be higher; Wheels observed 8.5 in one LS test.

boot.basis: VDA; second row occupied, third row folded; measured to second-row seatback, not to roof.

bootAllRows.basis: VDA to third-row seatback with all seven seats available.

length.basis: Original ZM body; excludes later facelift.

towing.basis: Maximum braked trailer; 160-kg towball limit. Verify actual payload, trailer and towbar ratings.

vehicles.warranty: Standard 5 years/100,000 km; conditional dealer-serviced extension up to 10 years/200,000 km. Confirm remaining cover by VIN and service history.
vehicles.servicing: 12 months/15,000 km, whichever first. Historical MY22/22.5 caps are not a new ten-year entitlement from your used-car purchase.

safety.applicability: Original ZM petrol LS is included. ANCAP lists July 2021–March 2025 builds; later facelift has separate applicability. Child-restraint fit is not established by the star rating.

familyFit.summary: BabyDrive fitted three forward-facing seats in the 2022 Exceed seven-seat. This LS transfer is provisional; your seats and buckle access remain unconfirmed.
familyFit.row2: Two outboard ISOFIX positions; top tethers for all three positions. Outer tethers are on seatbacks; centre tether is in the roof above row three.
familyFit.row3: No top tethers or ISOFIX. ANCAP does not recommend installing child restraints here. Do not treat seven seats as seven restraint positions.
familyFit.testedSeats: 2022 Exceed: Infasecure Achieve More, Aspire More and Attain More, all forward-facing. Different trim from this LS.
familyFit.buckleAccess: Buckles sit flush in the related test. ANCAP found one convertible and one booster incompatible in the centre; check your exact models.
familyFit.access: BabyDrive had to remove a row-two restraint before folding the seat for third-row access. Centre tether crosses the third-row passenger area.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear console vents for row two; no dedicated third-row vents. LS has dual-zone front climate control.

pros: Three forward-facing restraints reported in the related Exceed test.
478-L VDA boot with the third row folded.
91-RON petrol, 18-inch tyres and a 15,000-km service interval.
cons: Third-row child restraints are not recommended by ANCAP.
163-L VDA boot with all seven seats up; access requires moving a child seat.
Claimed 7.7 L/100km is above the hybrid alternatives in urban use.
inspection: Bring all three seats/boosters; check centre compatibility, independent buckle access and the roof-tether route.
Get written VIN confirmation of warranty eligibility and completed scheduled services, especially any fleet/rental history.
Check camera software campaigns REC-005692 and REC-005938 by VIN; applicable updates are free.
Test the CVT cold and hot for hesitation, shudder or noise; obtain diagnostic and service-history checks. No ZM failure rate is asserted.
Check actual screen, power tailgate and tyre placard: shortage-era equipment changed. Inspect spare, tyre wear and towing history.

changes.text: Groups the 2.5-litre FWD LS seven-seat drivetrain and original body. Does not include older ZL cars. Verify model year rather than relying on registration year.
The period LS road test records deletion of the powered tailgate during semiconductor shortages. Check the individual car rather than assuming higher-trim equipment.
Later facelift and new pricing are excluded from this original-body used cohort; late registrations need a build/model-year check.

gaps: No direct BabyDrive LS test or confirmation with your own three restraints.
MY25 facelift petrol LS needs a separate researched entry.
No credible Australian ZM LS repair-failure frequency or installed CVT replacement quote was verified.
Insurance and future servicing are estimates, not personal quotes.
Photo is a labelled Japan-market PHEV generation reference; it does not show the LS petrol trim.

vehicles.headline: Three-across evidence in a seven-seat T33; third-row restraints remain unsuitable.
vehicles.summary: Australian original ST AWD is the seven-seat petrol configuration; ST 2WD and e-POWER have different seating. BabyDrive fitted three mixed-direction seats in a seven-seat T33, with exact ST trim unconfirmed. Your fit check remains pending.

range.basis: Electric range does not apply to this petrol configuration.

battery.basis: No traction battery; conventional petrol drivetrain.

depletedConsumption.basis: Charge-depleted PHEV consumption does not apply.

vehicles.batteryWarranty: No high-voltage traction battery. Standard 12-V battery terms differ from the vehicle warranty.

consumption.basis: Manufacturer combined ADR 81/02 claim for 2.5 petrol AWD; not the 2WD 7.4 figure. Related ST-L AWD road test observed 8.9 in mixed driving.

boot.basis: Manufacturer seven-seat cargo figure with third row folded, measured to roof; not comparable directly with VDA-to-seatback figures.

bootAllRows.basis: No all-seven-up litre figure verified in Nissan Australian period specifications. Bring your actual pram.

width.basis: Manufacturer width INCLUDING mirrors; body-only width is not this figure. Keep measurement basis in comparisons.

towing.basis: Maximum braked trailer; petrol AWD rating. Verify towball, payload and fitted towbar limits.

vehicles.warranty: Standard 5 years/unlimited km. Eligible vehicles can gain dealer-service-activated cover up to 10 years/300,000 km; obtain written VIN-specific eligibility.
vehicles.servicing: MY23–MY25: 12 months/10,000 km, whichever first. At 15,000 km/year allow roughly 1.5 scheduled visits. MY26’s 15,000-km interval is excluded.

safety.applicability: T33 ST petrol AWD is covered; Australian launch November 2022. Based on Qashqai testing with additional X-Trail evidence, 2021 datestamp; listed expiry December 2027.

familyFit.summary: BabyDrive fitted three restraints across row two in a 2023 seven-seat T33. Tested grade is not confirmed as ST, and the combination included a rear-facing capsule.
familyFit.row2: Two outboard ISOFIX positions and three top tethers. Outer tethers are on seatbacks; centre tether is in the roof above row three.
familyFit.row3: No ISOFIX or top tethers. ANCAP does not recommend installing child restraints here; do not assume a third-row forward-facing seat or booster is suitable.
familyFit.testedSeats: Infasecure Achieve More + Momentum More forward-facing, with Adapt More capsule rear-facing. This does not confirm your three-forward-facing/booster arrangement.
familyFit.buckleAccess: No verified three-booster buckle-access test. ANCAP could not correctly install either tested booster in the centre, despite other tested seats fitting.
familyFit.access: BabyDrive needed to remove one of three row-two child seats for third-row access. Centre tether crosses the third-row passenger area.
familyFit.ventilation: Rear console vents for row two; no dedicated third-row vents. Base ST has manual air-conditioning, not the higher grades’ climate-control specification.

pros: Published three-across test in a seven-seat T33.
91-RON petrol, 17-inch tyres and a temporary spare.
Wide rear-door openings aid loading children in the related road test.
cons: Third-row child restraints are not recommended; some centre-row booster combinations fail ANCAP installation checks.
Original 10,000-km interval can mean more than one service each year.
Base ST lacks the ST-L’s surround-view camera and higher-grade comfort features.
inspection: Bring the exact restraints: test the centre seat, booster buckles, roof-tether route and entry with three installed.
Confirm the car is 2.5 petrol AWD seven-seat; ST 2WD and e-POWER are different configurations.
Request the VIN service-price schedule and written service-activated warranty status; check all original 10,000-km services.
Test CVT and AWD operation cold/hot, review fluid/maintenance records and inspect underbody/towing wear. Do not transfer old T32 failure rates to this T33.
Ask Nissan to check all campaigns by VIN. REC-006653 covers e-POWER, so it is not applied to this petrol car.
Confirm third-row protection and restraint guidance in the specific Australian manual; public curtain-airbag descriptions conflict.

changes.text: Groups original ST 2.5 petrol CVT AWD seven-seat. Excludes previous-generation T32, five-seat 2WD, e-POWER and higher grades.
Nissan announced a 12.3-inch ST screen with wireless phone mirroring and 15,000-km/12-month servicing. Excluded here because equipment and costs differ.

gaps: The exact BabyDrive test grade is unconfirmed; no verified three-forward-facing or three-booster combination for this ST.
No primary all-seven-seats-up cargo litre figure verified.
MY26 facelift ST AWD needs its own configuration and current price research.
No Australian T33 2.5-petrol failure frequency or installed CVT replacement quote verified.
ANCAP technical table and manufacturer/advert descriptions differ on third-row curtain coverage; confirm the VIN/manual.
Photo is an overseas e-POWER generation reference, not the ST petrol trim.

ownership.serviceBasis: A$450/year planning allowance at 15,000 km. Historical manufacturer MY22/22.5 ten-service schedule totals A$3,190 (A$319/year from new). A used purchase starts partway through that schedule; A$450 adds a buffer for later major services and time after the cap. MY23/24 pricing and remaining eligibility require a VIN quote. Excludes tyres and unscheduled repairs.
warrantyCautions: Standard 5-year/100,000-km cover is distinct from the conditional 10-year/200,000-km extension; the latter requires qualifying dealer servicing.
Ask Mitsubishi for written remaining coverage, original retail date and service eligibility. Do not rely solely on a used dealer’s ten-year advertising.
Normal wear, accident damage and skipped maintenance are not blanket warranty claims; Australian Consumer Law rights are separate.

risks.title: Camera/infotainment software recalls — free remedy
risks.detail: REC-005692 affects selected MY22/MY23 cars; REC-005938 affects selected MY22 cars. Both concern the reversing-camera display and specify free software updates. Check the VIN and completion record.
risks.priceBasis: Official recall remedy A$0; not an expected paid repair.
risks.warranty: Official campaign remedy is free for an affected VIN.

risks.title: CVT, engine and cooling-system exposure
risks.detail: These are potentially expensive systems once cover ends, but no credible ZM-specific Australian installed replacement quote or failure rate was verified. Cold/hot CVT operation, leaks, maintenance records and diagnostic codes are inspection checks, not a claim of a known epidemic.
risks.priceBasis: Not priced: obtain diagnosis and a model-specific installed quote. No PHEV traction-battery allowance is applied to this petrol car.
risks.warranty: Manufacturing faults may qualify under the remaining standard/conditional warranty; wear and maintenance exclusions apply.

risks.title: Age-related suspension — Australian workshop proxy
risks.detail: A repairer’s conventional front damper-pair guide quotes A$650–1,300 including labour. This is a generic Australian budgeting example, not a ZM quote or proof this repair will occur.
risks.priceBasis: AUD installed generic front damper pair; diagnosis, alignment or extra components may add cost.
risks.warranty: Wear is normally outside manufacturing-defect cover; obtain a vehicle-specific decision.

ownership.serviceInterval: Original MY23–MY25: 12 months / 10,000 km, whichever comes first
ownership.serviceBasis: A$650/year planning allowance at 15,000 km. A 2023 petrol AWD road test quoted a five-service prepay total of A$2,124: A$424.80/visit × roughly 1.5 visits/year = A$637.20, rounded with a small buffer. This is a historical related-ST-L AWD reference, not a current ST quote. Nissan’s A$399 first-five-services offer is restricted to vehicles retailed new from January 2025; older retail dates need a VIN schedule. Excludes wear and unscheduled repairs.
warrantyCautions: Standard 5-year/unlimited-kilometre cover is distinct from service-activated cover up to 10 years/300,000 km. Eligible used vehicles need documented history and written Nissan confirmation.
The activation program includes qualifying vehicles first sold new from January 2021, subject to its servicing conditions; do not assume every private or ex-fleet purchase retains maximum cover.
MY26’s longer 15,000-km service interval does not apply to this MY23–MY25 cohort.

risks.title: CVT and AWD repair exposure — price unverified
risks.detail: Both systems can create a substantial bill outside cover. No credible Australian installed T33 2.5-petrol replacement quote or failure frequency was verified. Inspect cold/hot operation, leaks and servicing. Older T32 or overseas 1.5-turbo Rogue evidence is not transferred to this engine/generation.
risks.priceBasis: Unpriced scenario; request a VIN-specific diagnosis and installed quote. The savings allowance is not an expected annual claim cost.
risks.warranty: A manufacturing defect may be covered if standard or service-activated warranty remains valid; wear and neglect are excluded.

risks.title: Age-related suspension — Australian workshop proxy
risks.detail: Generic conventional front damper-pair replacement is quoted at A$650–1,300 with labour by an Australian repairer. This is not a T33 quote or an incidence estimate.
risks.priceBasis: AUD installed generic front damper pair; alignment and additional components may cost extra.
risks.warranty: Normal wear can be excluded; ask Nissan to assess a manufacturing defect.

insurance.basis: A$1,160 is the rounded midpoint of Youi’s published A$785–1,531 Outlander premium range, not a reported mean. Policies sold 22 November 2025–22 May 2026; 80% fell within or below that range. Includes mixed years/powertrains and Australia-wide risks, not this LS or your Queensland address. A$780–2,500 is an analyst planning range, not an insurer interval. Replace with your comprehensive quote; CTP is in rego separately.

Rounded from Youi’s published A$1,181 X-Trail comprehensive mean; A$744–1,521 indicative range. Policies sold 22 November 2025–22 May 2026; model averages require at least ten policies, and 80% fell within or below the range. Mixed generations/powertrains, not an ST AWD Queensland quote. A$740–2,500 planning bounds are analyst assumptions. Replace with your quote; CTP is separate.

tyres.basis: Original LS 18-inch fitment. JAX 235/60R18 107V XL Goodyear Optilife 3 SUV: A$259 each fitted including GST, four A$1036; no temporary multi-buy discount assumed. Confirm placard load/speed rating, local stock and quote; alignment extra. Life 45,000 km (35,000–60,000) and set-price bounds are analyst assumptions, not measured model-specific tyre life.

Original ST 17-inch fitment. JAX 235/65R17 108V XL Michelin Primacy 5: A$329 each fitted including GST, four A$1316; no temporary multi-buy discount assumed. Confirm placard load/speed rating, local stock and quote; alignment extra. Life 45,000 km (35,000–60,000) and set-price bounds are analyst assumptions, not measured model-specific tyre life.

repairReserves.basis: Analyst repair-savings allowance: A$750/year, with A$350–1,600 sensitivity bounds. For an original 2022–24 petrol LS bought used and retained long term; cover may expire during ownership. Anchored to conditional warranty terms and generic Australian installed suspension work, not model-specific claims frequency. This is money set aside, not predicted annual spending. No traction-battery reserve; tyres and scheduled servicing are separate. Prior condition, service history and confirmed coverage matter more than this point estimate.

Analyst repair-savings allowance: A$800/year, A$350–1,800 sensitivity bounds, for original T33 petrol AWD retained long term. Allows for uncertain post-warranty mechanical/electronic work and AWD complexity; no credible failure-rate dataset supports a precise ranking against Outlander or Tesla. Warranty conditions and generic Australian installed suspension costs are context, not actuarial inputs. No e-POWER battery reserve. Tyres, scheduled services and insured crash costs are separate; replace with your own buffer. This is not an observed average repair bill.

expertReviews.scope: Exact grade/powertrain road test; one review, not a reliability survey. Rating was awarded in 2022.
expertReviews.verdict: The LS test found a comfortable, good-value urban family car, with a small and awkward third row.
negativeThemes: Cramped third row and difficult access

expertReviews.scope: Related higher ST-L trim, not this ST; cabin options differ. Publisher now shows a categorical Good verdict, so no numeric score is invented.
expertReviews.verdict: The related seven-seat petrol AWD test praised refinement and packaging; row three was best for occasional use and the short service interval added cost.
positiveThemes: Spacious second row and wide rear doors
negativeThemes: Some equipment omissions for the price
